slot.subtopic: Diagonal relationship of Li and Mg
slot.brief: Which properties of Li resemble Mg rather than other alkali metals (nitride formation, carbonate decomposition); pick the correct set of shared properties.

stem: Which statements correctly describe similarities between lithium and magnesium? I. Both form nitrides on direct combination with nitrogen. II. Both carbonates decompose on heating to the oxide and carbon dioxide. III. Both hydroxides are highly soluble in water. IV. Both form superoxides on reaction with oxygen.

verdicts.working: Li and Mg both form nitrides directly with nitrogen, and both carbonates decompose on heating to the oxide and CO₂. Mg(OH)₂ is sparingly soluble, and neither forms a superoxide with oxygen. Thus I and II are correct.

working:
$\text{Li}_3\text{N}$ and $\text{Mg}_3\text{N}_2$ form by direct combination with $\text{N}_2$.
$\text{Li}_2\text{CO}_3\xrightarrow{\Delta}\text{Li}_2\text{O}+\text{CO}_2$; $\text{MgCO}_3\xrightarrow{\Delta}\text{MgO}+\text{CO}_2$.
III and IV are false. Independent check: Li and Mg both form nitrides directly with nitrogen, and both carbonates decompose on heating to the oxide and CO₂. Mg(OH)₂ is sparingly soluble, and neither forms a superoxide with oxygen. Thus I and II are correct.
solution:
Both combine directly with nitrogen to form nitrides: Li₃N and Mg₃N₂.
$$\text{Li}_2\text{CO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Li}_2\text{O}+\text{CO}_2,\qquad \text{MgCO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{MgO}+\text{CO}_2$$
Mg(OH)₂ is sparingly soluble, and neither metal forms a superoxide; hence only I and II are correct.
